chapter: Pictures, Oliver, Armstrong and Fat Pichon
title: Arthur's photo of his father and the Peerless band 1906 picture
summary: Arthur kept an old photograph of his father; they discuss another Peerless band picture from about 1906 that might show him.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Hunting for old band photographs and scrapbooks

blocks.x: Now this is a picture that honestly, my daddy's picture, that's an old picture, you can see that. Now, this picture was in the latest house on St. Louis, a place where my father kept these horses. When he had his shower on, many years ago. And I found that picture up there. I seen that picture up there and I took it. And I kept the picture, I said, I'm going to take this picture, I said, that's my daddy on there. And I kept the picture away from him and I carried it to my house. And I've been nursing that picture ever since. And that's been many years ago. And I just kept that picture and saved it, you know, just because he was on it. It's a good picture. And my sisters never wanted it. And they said, let it to me, I'm going to have some men like it, I want to get one of it. You know, after you get to a certain age, you can, my sister's younger than me, she doesn't remember my dad as well as I did, you see. I want to get his picture made. And I went on and I promised to tell her, but I never did give it to her. And then I loaned it to her one time, at the time of year again. She bent it in half. Bent it in half and everything else. That's why I never didn't want to give it to her. Well, at that time she wouldn't get the picture made. I know she wanted it for something. She'd come in, she'd beg, but she said, I'll take it, I'll bring it back. I said, all right. Then when you came, it wasn't here, I had to go get it for me. You remember that?
Yeah. Well, I glued it back together. It's in shape again.

Well, we have another one now. And now my sister was here today. She saw the large medium. She said, well, where did you get that at? She said, don't you have another one? I said, I have the old one. Well, what do you want to do with two of them? Now she's trying to get one, you see. Yeah, we'll give it that one. No, this one's for my little sister.
Oh, that's the other one. That's the younger sister. I'll get you another print. I have another print. I'm Kevin.
Okay. You know, there was another picture of the Pure List band. It was a different drummer, though.
What's it? I don't know.
All I saw was the negatives, so I couldn't really tell. I didn't see the print. Yeah, I don't remember now. I have to check. It was published in Esquire. Yeah. I tried it, but. 1945.
Mm-hmm. Oh, well, in 1945, that would have had to be another drum in there. No, no, no.
It was an old picture. It was just penned there. Oh, oh, that was published. It must have been a 1906 picture, even.
Oh, yeah.
I can't remember. I have to check on that. It might be your father on that.
Well, you have it at your shop, the big negative.

Yeah, I have it. I have it. I can make a credit. We got it from Maurice Durand, who just died last week on Thanksgiving Day. Oh, yeah. A carnet player. Used to live way downtown in Ninth Warden. He went to California. He died just last week. But he had a picture of the Peerless Band. It had Bab Frank on it, too. And on the drum was written, Frank and McCurdy or something, Peerless Band, 1906. But that date might have been put on the picture. I don't know. I don't think it was really on the drum. I think somebody wrote it on the picture. Okay. It was taken about 1906. Yeah. So it's likely your father was on that, too, I think.
Yeah. It might have been 1906. He was with the band around that.
We can tell if it looks like this picture of your father here. Oh, you don't know.
Who was the drum on it?
No, I'm not real sure.
Oh, I see. I did know.
Somebody went over it with me. I should know if I see the picture. We could tell right away.
Yeah, if I see it, I could tell if that's him.
I'll try to get you a print of it sometime then. Okay. If it is your father, we'll try to get another print made up.
If I don't get down here, I'll mail you the other print.
